attacks.claim: The embargo badge text is hard-coded #ffffff on background var(--surface), which is #ffffff in the default light theme. The label is invisible in light mode and fails WCAG 1.4.3 contrast, a stated release requirement. The hard-coded color is the root cause, since it bypasses theme tokens.

The unpublish control is a <span> with only onClick: no role, tabIndex, or keyboard handler, and the icon is aria-hidden so it has no accessible name. Keyboard-only and screen-reader editors cannot reach, operate, or identify this destructive action (WCAG 2.1.1, 4.1.2). There is also no :focus-visible style.

handleUnpublish awaits onUnpublish with no try/catch, no error feedback, and no pending or disabled state. A failed call is an unhandled rejection, and the editor may believe a time-sensitive takedown succeeded. Repeat clicks can fire duplicate requests.
attacks.evidence: if (ok) await onUnpublish(draft.id);  (no try/catch, no loading state)

attacks.claim: The UI shows unpublish on every published row, and the diff does not show a server-side permission check or audit logging for the endpoint behind onUnpublish. This is likely enforced in the existing API, which is outside this diff, so it is a verification note rather than a defect shown here.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: role/permission check or audit logging for onUnpublish in the diff

attacks.claim: The embargo lift time is formatted without a timezone designator, so editors outside the newsroom zone or comparing against wire times could misread it. The formatter's implementation is not in the diff.
The embargo state comes from the client clock at render time with no re-render trigger, so it can be stale or skewed. The PR also calls the action 'one-click' though it opens a confirm dialog.
